items.title: Intel’s 45% Downturn Over 3 Months Unsettles Investors: This Wall Street Analyst Predicts 155% Gains Anyway
items.summary: Intel just posted its best server quarter in 15 years, yet the stock cratered anyway. One analyst still sees a path to more than double from here, while others see a turnaround with no committed customers. Who is reading the data right?

items.title: Risky Nvidia Is Cheaper Than 'Safe' Walmart
items.summary: Everyone knows the cast: Nvidia is the AI growth stock, and Walmart and Costco are the safe places to hide. Nvidia reports today, Tuesday, Nov 17, with its results call set for 2 p.m. Going in, the labels have swapped on one count that matters: price against next year's earnings.

items.title: Qualcomm CEO: “There Is No AI Correction” at Qualcomm. Nvidia’s November 17 Earnings Face a Major Test
items.summary: Key TakeawaysQualcomm (QCOM) CEO Cristiano Amon said there is no AI correction at his company, citing strong semiconductor demand and industrywide supply shortages despite the recent technology selloff. NVIDIA (NVDA) faces its November 17 earnings report following Jensen Huang’s resignation, with investors watching whether AI infrastructure demand can sustain its aggressive growth forecasts.

items.title: What Is Qualcomm (QCOM) Gaining From Its Cockpit And SoOp Momentum?
items.summary: Qualcomm (NasdaqGS:QCOM) reports growing traction for its Snapdragon intelligent cockpit SoCs in new vehicle programs across global automakers. The company is increasingly referenced by industry groups as a core supplier in the emerging signals of opportunity, or SoOp, navigation market. Government and defense agencies are exploring SoOp systems that pair advanced Qualcomm silicon with AI for autonomous and GPS limited settings.
